title: Media and Press Freedom
description: Understanding constitutional guarantees for media freedom and press rights in Nepal.

sections.title: Constitutional Basis
sections.content: Freedom of the press is an extension of freedom of expression, enabling journalists and media institutions to publish without undue censorship. The Constitution safeguards editorial independence and prohibits prior restraint except under narrowly defined circumstances.
keyPoints: Press freedom linked to expression rights
Prohibits prior restraint except limited cases

sections.title: Responsibilities and Ethics
sections.content: While enjoying freedom, media actors must adhere to accuracy, fairness, and ethical standards. Self-regulation through codes of conduct builds public trust and counters misinformation.

sections.title: Regulatory and Legal Framework
sections.content: Broadcast, print, and digital media may be subject to licensing, content standards, and ownership transparency rules. Laws address defamation, incitement, and national security while striving not to chill legitimate reporting.

sections.title: Digital Era Challenges
sections.content: Online platforms accelerate news distribution but raise challenges: fake news propagation, algorithmic bias, and pressures on traditional revenue models. Digital literacy and platform accountability measures help sustain an informed public sphere.

summary: Digital changes create new accountability challenges
